nodes.name: Electrochemical plating of PANI
nodes.procedure: HCl (8mL) + water (87.5mL) + aniline (4.5mL) was used as electrolyte. Graphite rod and Ag/AgCl (in saturated KCl) were used as counter electrode and reference electrode, respectively. A cleaned carbon paper was used as working electrode and the electroplating area was 1×1 cm². The electroplating voltage was 1.0 V and the electroplating time was 10 min. After that, carbon paper was washed with water and dried at 60°C in a vacuum oven.
nodes.source_text: The Co SAC@CP was prepared by a modified electrochemical plating method [38]. HCl (8mL) + water (87.5mL) + aniline (4.5mL) was used as electrolyte... dried at 60°C in a vacuum oven. The slice was labeled as PANI@CP.

nodes.name: Co SAC synthesis
nodes.procedure: The PANI@CP was immersed into CoCl2 solution (0.1M) and placed for 4h in room temperature. Subsequently, the slice was token out and dried. The dried slice was placed in a tubular furnace, and the temperature was raised to 750°C in a rate of 2°C/min and kept at the temperature for 3h in a Ar gas flow. After treatment with 1.0M H2SO4 at room temperature for 24h, the black slice was taken out, dried and labeled as Co SAC@CP.

nodes.name: CoFe DAC synthesis
nodes.procedure: The above Co SAC@CP catalyst was put into a tubular furnace, with 0.4 mmol ferrous chloride hexahydrate (FeCl2·6H2O) at the upstream of the stream. Then the temperature was raised up to 700°C in a rate of 2°C/min and keep for 2h. After that, the temperature was raised to 750°C for 2°C/min and kept at 750°C for 1h. The obtained black slice was pickling in 5.0M H2SO4 for 24h at room temperature. After cleaning and drying, the obtained black slice was labeled as CoFe DAC@CP.

nodes.name: CoCu DAC synthesis
nodes.procedure: The above Co SAC@CP catalyst was put into a tubular furnace, with 0.4 mmol copper acetate monohydrate(Cu (CO2CH3)2 H2O) at the upstream of the stream. Then the temperature was raised up to 250°C in a rate of 2°C/min and keep for 2h. After that, the temperature was raised to 750°C for 2°C/min and kept at 750°C for 1h. The obtained black slice was pickling in 5.0M H2SO4 for 24h at room temperature. After cleaning and drying, the obtained black slice was labeled as CoCu DAC@CP.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images show short rod-like shape on carbon paper for all catalysts (CoFe DAC, CoCu DAC, CoZn DAC, Co SAC).
nodes.evidence_snippet: SEM and TEM images of the CoFe DAC indicate that it's short rod-like shape on the carbon paper (Figs. 2b-c, S4) ... The prepared CoCu DAC, CoZn DAC and Co SAC also show similar short rod-like structures without nanoparticles (Figs. S7-S10).

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM and HRTEM images show no metal particles observed, implying mono-dispersion of metal atoms for all catalysts.
nodes.evidence_snippet: no metal particles are observed in HRTEM images (Fig. 2d-e), implying the mono-dispersion of metal atoms ... The prepared CoCu DAC, CoZn DAC and Co SAC also show similar short rod-like structures without nanoparticles (Figs. S7-S10).

nodes.characterization_summary: Aberration-corrected HAADF-STEM shows dual-atom pairs with Co-Fe distance of 0.22 nm in CoFe DAC.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Aberration-corrected high-angle annular dark-field STEM (HAADF-STEM) image in Fig. 2f-g clearly demonstrates the existence of dual-atom pairs... Statistical analysis of dual atoms showed a Co-Fe distance of 0.22 nm

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS elemental mapping reveals C, N, Co and Fe distributed evenly in CoFe DAC.
nodes.evidence_snippet: HAADF-STEM (Fig. 2h) and elemental mapping (Fig. 2i) reveal that C, N, Co and Fe are distributed evenly in CoFe DAC.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns exhibit two characteristic diffraction peaks at 26.5° and 54.6° ascribed to graphite (111) and (222) planes, no metal or metal oxides peaks observed.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The CoCu, CoFe, CoZn DAC@CP and Co SAC@CP all exhibit two characteristic diffraction peaks in X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns at about 26.5° and 54.6° ... No metal or metal oxides diffraction peaks are observed.

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman spectra show D band at 1350 cm⁻¹ and G band at 1580 cm⁻¹; ID/IG ratios of 1.01, 0.98, 0.96 for CoCu, CoFe, CoZn DAC indicate intense carbon defects.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Raman spectra (Fig. S12) show typical carbon peaks at about 1350 cm⁻¹ (D band) and 1580 cm⁻¹ (G band) ... The ratio ID/IG of CoCu DAC@CP, CoFe DAC@CP and CoZn DAC@CP are 1.01, 0.98 and 0.96, respectively

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS shows C1s (sp² C at 284.8 eV, sp³ C at 285.7 eV), N1s (pyridinic N 398.4 eV, metal-N 399.7 eV), and positive valence states of Co/Cu/Fe/Zn metals; higher Metal-N content in DACs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) of CoCu, CoFe and CoZn DAC@CP shows C1s, N1s, O1s, Co2p and Cu2p/Fe2p/Zn2p peaks ... The C1s spectrum shows sp² C (284.8 eV), sp³ C (285.7 eV) ... The 2p signals of Co/Cu/Fe/Zn imply positive valence state

nodes.characterization_summary: Co K-edge XANES shows absorption edge shifted ~3.0 eV lower than CoO, indicating Co valence between Co⁰⁺ and Co²⁺; Fe K-edge similar to FePC.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The absorption edge of Co K-edge for CoCu, CoFe, CoZn DAC@CP and Co SAC@CP are all shifted ~3.0 eV towards lower energy relative to CoO ... The absorption edge of Fe K-edge of CoFe DAC@CP was similar to that of FePC

nodes.characterization_summary: Fourier-transform EXAFS shows Co-N (~1.50 Å), Co-M/Co-C (~2.30 Å) for DACs; Fe-N (1.47 Å), Fe-M/Fe-C (2.27 Å) for CoFe DAC, confirming dual-atomic structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In Co EXAFS spectra of the Co-M dual-atom catalysts (Fig. 3c), the peaks at ~1.50 Å and ~2.30 Å are ascribed to the Co-N and Co-M/Co-C coordination ... the main peak at 1.47 Å and 2.27 Å in Fe EXAFS spectra of CoFe DAC (Fig. 3d) are ascribed to Fe-N coordination and Fe-M/Fe-C coordination
